title: Adding Principal to a Certificate of Deposit During Its Term
content:
Outside the grace period, most tiers of the Certificates of Deposit line take no further principal at all. One tier does, and this bulletin states the figures.

| Tier | Most deposits accepted during a term, outside grace | Smallest single deposit, USD | Most added in total during one term, USD |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | 0 | not applicable | not applicable |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | 0 | not applicable | not applicable |
| 12-Month Certificate | 0 | not applicable | not applicable |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | 1 | 100.00 | 25000.00 |
| 36-Month Certificate | 0 | not applicable | not applicable |
| 60-Month Certificate | 0 | not applicable | not applicable |

The 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate is the single tier that accepts a deposit while its term is running. It accepts one such deposit in a term, of at least 100.00 USD, and no more than 25000.00 USD in total across the term.

Because the tier accepts exactly 1 deposit in a term, the figure of 25000.00 USD for the term total and the figure for the single deposit bind on the same sum where the allowance is used once.

The five tiers showing 0 show "not applicable" in both amount columns: there is no small deposit that would be let through on them, since the count itself is nil.
